title: PATH-Bench: Path-Dependent Evaluation of Lifelong Agents
abstract: arXiv:2608.01149v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Lifelong LLM agents increasingly adapt through external learning states that store past interactions as retrievable memories or reusable skills, yet existing benchmarks rarely account for how the path of accumulated experience shapes what agents transfer and retain. In this work, we establish PATH-Bench, a benchmark for path-dependent evaluation of lifelong agents. PATH-Bench estimates directed task relationships via multi-model in-context learning, constructs probe-centered sequences with controlled helpful and interfering histories, and repeatedly evaluates probe tasks to measure average performance, forward transfer, backward transfer, and forgetting. We evaluate eight representative agents on single-turn code generation and multi-turn tool-use tasks under positive- and negative-dominant histories. Benchmark results show that experience utility depends jointly on how experience is represented and on the task's interaction structur

translated_title: PATH-Bench：终身智能体的路径依赖评估
translated_abstract: 终身学习的大语言模型智能体越来越多地通过外部学习状态进行适应，这些状态将过去的交互存储为可检索的记忆或可复用的技能，然而现有基准很少考虑累积经验的路径如何塑造智能体能够迁移和保留的内容。在这项工作中，我们建立了PATH-Bench，一个用于终身智能体路径依赖评估的基准。PATH-Bench通过多模型上下文学习估计有向任务关系，构建以探测任务为中心且带有受控有益历史和干扰历史的序列，并反复评估探测任务以衡量平均性能、前向迁移、后向迁移和遗忘。我们在正向主导和负向主导的历史条件下，评估了八个代表性智能体在单轮代码生成和多轮工具使用任务上的表现。基准结果表明，经验的效用同时取决于经验的表示方式以及任务的交互结构。
tldr: 该论文提出PATH-Bench，首个对终身智能体进行路径依赖评估的基准，通过构建带有受控有益与干扰历史的任务序列来测量平均性能、前向/后向迁移和遗忘，揭示经验效用同时取决于经验的表示方式与任务的交互结构。
en_tdlr: PATH-Bench is a path-dependent evaluation benchmark for lifelong agents that constructs probe-centered sequences with controlled helpful and interfering histories to measure average performance, forward/backward transfer, and forgetting, revealing that experience utility depends jointly on how experience is represented and the task's interaction structure.
